questions.question:
A. First, volunteers gathered at the basketball court and were given gloves and sacks.
B. Our barangay held a clean-up drive last Saturday.
C. Finally, the captain thanked everyone and promised to hold the drive monthly.
D. After that, they sorted the collected trash into recyclables and waste.
E. Then they split into groups and swept each street. What should be the 2nd sentence?
questions.explanation: A is the 2nd sentence. Correct order: B-A-E-D-C.

questions.explanation: D is the 3rd sentence. Correct order: E-B-D-C-A.

questions.question:
Which sentence best fits the blank?
____ Mangoes are sweet, bananas are rich in potassium, and papayas aid digestion.
options: Tropical fruits offer both flavor and nutrition.
Potassium is found only in bananas.
questions.explanation: The details name tastes and health benefits of different fruits, so the topic sentence covers them all.

questions.question:
What is the main idea of the paragraph?
Many Filipinos travel by jeepney because it is cheap and runs along most routes. Riders can hop on and off almost anywhere. Its open design even lets passengers chat with strangers.
options: Jeepneys are painted in bright colors.
The jeepney is a convenient and affordable form of transport.
Strangers should not talk to each other.
questions.explanation: Every detail (low fare, many routes, easy boarding) supports the jeepney's convenience and affordability.

questions.question:
Which sentence would be the best topic sentence?
____ Lack of sleep makes it hard to concentrate, weakens the immune system, and puts drivers at risk of accidents.
options: Getting too little sleep harms both health and safety.
Beds are available in many sizes.
questions.explanation: The supporting details are harms to health and safety, so the topic sentence must name them.

questions.question:
Which title best expresses the main idea of the paragraph?
Before refrigerators were invented, people kept food from spoiling by salting, smoking, and drying it. Fishermen dried fish under the sun, and families pickled vegetables in vinegar.
questions.explanation: Salting, smoking, drying and pickling are all methods of preserving food; the paragraph is not about refrigerators.

questions.question:
Which sentence best fits the blank?
____ For example, a plastic bag may be used for a few seconds, but it can last hundreds of years in the soil.
options: Soil is needed to grow rice.
Plastic waste stays in the environment for a very long time.
questions.explanation: "For example" introduces an illustration of long-lasting plastic waste, which the topic sentence must state.

questions.question:
What is the main idea of the paragraph?
Some people think that talent alone makes a great pianist. Yet most famous musicians practiced for hours every day from childhood. Their success came less from natural gift than from steady effort.
options: Talent is all that is needed.
Consistent practice matters more than talent for musical success.
questions.explanation: The paragraph rejects the talent-only view and stresses steady effort.

questions.question:
Which sentence is the topic sentence of the paragraph?
(1) The bahay kubo is designed to suit the tropical climate. (2) Its raised floor keeps out floods and animals. (3) Its woven walls let air pass through. (4) Its roof of palm leaves sheds heavy rain.
questions.explanation: Sentence 1 states the general idea; sentences 2-4 give specific design features that support it.

questions.question:
Which sentence best fits the blank?
____ A lighthouse warns ships of rocks, a siren warns villagers of floods, and a flashing light warns drivers of danger.
questions.explanation: All three examples are warning signals, so the general idea is that signals protect people from danger.

questions.question:
What is the main idea of the paragraph?
A student who borrows a classmate's notes should return them promptly. Lending notes is an act of trust, and keeping them too long may leave the owner unprepared for the exam. Returning them with thanks shows respect.
options: Borrowed notes should be returned promptly and gratefully.
questions.explanation: Each sentence supports returning borrowed notes quickly and with thanks.

questions.question:
Which sentence best states the main idea of the paragraph?
Although many believe goldfish have a three-second memory, experiments show they can recognize feeding times, find their way through mazes, and remember trained tasks for months.
options: Goldfish have far better memories than people assume.
Mazes are used to feed fish.
Memory lasts three seconds in all animals.
questions.explanation: The experiments contradict the common belief and show goldfish remember well.

questions.question:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) Volcanoes form when molten rock rises through cracks in the earth's crust. (2) The pressure can build up until the rock bursts out as lava. (3) My cousin took a train to Naga last year. (4) The lava cools and hardens, slowly building a mountain.
questions.explanation: Sentence 3 is about a train trip, not about how volcanoes form.

questions.question:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. (2) They require little maintenance once installed. (3) Many roofs in the city are painted red. (4) Over time, they can reduce a family's power bill.
questions.explanation: Sentence 3 describes roof color and does not discuss solar panels.

questions.question:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) Adopting a pet teaches children responsibility. (2) Feeding and walking an animal every day builds discipline. (3) Dogs have been companions to people for thousands of years. (4) Caring for a living thing also encourages kindness.
questions.explanation: Sentence 3 gives history of dogs, while the others list what children learn from owning a pet.

questions.question:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) The marathon begins at dawn to avoid the afternoon heat. (2) Runners receive water at every two kilometers. (3) Medical teams wait at the finish line. (4) The price of running shoes has increased this year.
questions.explanation: Sentence 4 is about shoe prices; the others describe how the race protects runners.

questions.question:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) The mayor is planning a new road. (2) Bees communicate through dancing. (3) The dance shows other bees where flowers are. (4) The angle of the dance tells the direction of the food.
questions.explanation: Sentence 1 is about a road; sentences 2-4 all explain how bees communicate.

questions.question:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) Typhoons are given names by weather agencies. (2) Using names makes warnings easier to remember. (3) Clear names help people share information quickly during emergencies. (4) A simple name can be understood across languages.
questions.explanation: Every sentence supports the idea that naming typhoons makes communication easier.

questions.question:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) Learning a second language improves memory. (2) Bilingual people often switch tasks more easily. (3) Studies show it may delay age-related mental decline. (4) Some bakeries open at midnight.
questions.explanation: Sentence 4 is about bakeries and has no link to the benefits of learning a language.

questions.question:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) A good leader listens before deciding. (2) Pineapples grow best in sandy soil. (3) Listening helps a leader understand the team's concerns. (4) Decisions made with input are more likely to be accepted.
questions.explanation: Sentence 2 is about farming, not about leadership.

questions.question:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into mountains by hand. (2) Ifugao farmers built them over many centuries. (3) Stone walls hold the soil in place on every level. (4) Today, they are a World Heritage Site that draws visitors.
questions.explanation: All sentences describe the rice terraces, so none is off-topic.

questions.question:
Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
(1) Online shopping saves time because stores are open at all hours. (2) Buyers can compare prices from many sellers within minutes. (3) Public libraries lend books for free. (4) Delivery lets shoppers receive goods without leaving home.
questions.explanation: Sentence 3 is about libraries, while the others list advantages of online shopping.

questions.question:
Choose the best transition.
The road was flooded. ____, we had to take a longer route.
questions.explanation: The longer route is the effect of the flood, so a cause-effect transition fits.

questions.question:
Choose the best transition.
Jose loves basketball. ____, his brother prefers swimming.
questions.explanation: The two brothers' preferences differ, so a contrast transition is needed.

questions.question:
Choose the best transition.
Many birds fly south in winter. ____, the swallow travels over 10,000 kilometers each way.
questions.explanation: The second sentence gives a specific case of the first, which "For example" introduces.

questions.question:
Choose the best transition.
Rain is expected tomorrow. ____, bring an umbrella.
questions.explanation: Bringing an umbrella is a result of the forecast.

questions.question:
Choose the best transition.
Wash your hands before cooking. ____, germs may spread to the food.
questions.explanation: "Otherwise" states what happens if the instruction is not followed.

questions.question:
Choose the best transition.
He trained for months. ____, he lost the race.
questions.explanation: Losing despite training is unexpected, so a contrast word is required.

questions.question: Which transition word signals that an example will follow?
questions.explanation: "For instance" introduces an example.

questions.question: Which transition word best signals a contrast?
questions.explanation: "On the other hand" presents an opposing point; the others show similarity, addition, result or example.

questions.question:
Choose the best transition.
The chef chopped the onions. ____, he fried them in oil. Finally, he added the tomatoes.
questions.explanation: "Next" continues the sequence between the first step and "Finally".

questions.question:
Choose the best transition.
The new bridge reduces travel time. ____, it makes the town safer by providing an escape route during floods.
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another benefit, so an addition word fits.

questions.question:
Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
Reading daily improves vocabulary and sharpens focus. It also reduces stress and sparks imagination. ____
options: Books are sold in many stores.
Reading glasses are sold in pharmacies.
In short, a daily reading habit enriches the mind.
questions.explanation: A conclusion sums up the benefits; the others add unrelated facts.

questions.question:
Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
Walking to school saves money on fare and keeps children active. It also lets them enjoy fresh air and chat with friends. ____
options: Thus, walking to school benefits a child's wallet and health.
Shoes should be replaced every year.
questions.explanation: The conclusion restates the benefits already given.

questions.question:
Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
Some critics say the new curfew punishes the innocent. Yet police report that accidents involving minors fell by half since it began. ____
options: Police should never speak to minors.
On balance, the curfew appears to have made young people safer.
Accidents have nothing to do with night.
The curfew should be ended immediately.
questions.explanation: It weighs both views and follows the evidence given, the drop in accidents.

questions.question:
Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
Ferries connect thousands of islands, carrying goods and passengers where bridges cannot reach. ____
options: Hence, ferries are vital to life in an archipelago.
questions.explanation: The conclusion draws the general importance of ferries from the detail.

questions.question:
Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
A single tree absorbs carbon dioxide, shades homes, and shelters birds. ____
options: Therefore, planting trees helps people and nature alike.
questions.explanation: It sums up the benefits and points to an action that follows.

questions.question:
Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
The experiment was repeated five times with different groups, and each result matched the first. ____
options: These consistent results strongly support the original conclusion.
questions.explanation: The conclusion states what the repeated, matching results prove.

questions.question:
Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
Good manners cost nothing but earn respect. Saying "po" and "opo" shows regard for elders, and thanking others builds friendship. ____
questions.explanation: It generalizes from the examples of courtesy.

questions.question:
Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
Early sailors used the stars to find direction at night. They also studied the wind and the waves. ____
options: Thus, ancient sailors relied on nature to guide their voyages.
Ships are now built of steel.
questions.explanation: The conclusion summarizes how sailors used natural signs.

questions.question:
Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
Sleeping late, skipping breakfast, and cramming at the last minute all lower exam scores. ____
options: Some students stay up to watch films.
Good study habits, not last-minute effort, lead to better results.
questions.explanation: It draws the lesson implied by the poor habits listed.

questions.question:
Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
Not only does volunteering help those in need, but it also gives the volunteer new skills and friends. ____
options: Skills are learned only in school.
Volunteering therefore benefits both the giver and the receiver.
questions.explanation: The conclusion combines the two benefits stated.
